rows.stdout:
Rust-based LPM client. Fast, correct, registry-aware.

Usage: lpm-baseline [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  info             Show package information
  search           Search for packages
  quality          Show quality report for a package
  whoami           Show who you're logged in as
  health           Check registry health
  download         Download and extract a package tarball
  fetch            Download packages from lpm.lock into the store without installing
  tidy             Report unused dependencies and undeclared imports
  resolve          Resolve dependency tree for packages
  install          Install dependencies from package.json, or add specific packages. [aliases: i]
  uninstall        Remove packages from dependencies and node_modules [aliases: un, unlink]
  add              Add source files from a package into your project (shadcn-style)
  publish          Publish a package to the LPM registry [aliases: p]
  version          Bump package.json version, optionally committing and tagging it
  release          Plan, apply, or publish a workspace release
  stage            Stage packages for npm publishing
  login            Log in to a package registry [aliases: l]
  logout           Log out from a package registry [aliases: lo]
  setup            Configure project `.npmrc` for CI or local development
  token-rotate     Rotate your auth token
  outdated         Check for newer versions of direct dependencies
  upgrade          Upgrade outdated LPM dependencies to latest versions
  init             Initialize a new package
  config           Manage CLI configuration
  policy           Inspect and test install-time policy extensions
  security         Manage temporary approvals for guarded security weakeners
  cache            Manage ephemeral caches under ~/.lpm/cache/ (metadata, tasks, dlx, mcp) and prune the global package store under ~/.lpm/store/
  store            Manage the global content-addressable package store
  catalog          Inspect workspace catalog usage and resolved catalog provenance
  global           Manage globally-installed CLI packages under ~/.lpm/global/
  trust            Inspect and manage project package trust and release-age exclusions
  pool             Show pool revenue stats
  skills           Manage Agent Skills
  remove           Remove a source-delivered package (reverse of `add`) [aliases: rm]
  audit            Audit installed packages for security/quality issues
  query            Query installed packages using CSS-like selectors
  licenses         Inventory installed dependency licenses and enforce policy gates
  rebuild          Execute dependency lifecycle scripts for installed packages (phase 2 of install)
  doctor           Health check: verify project state, runtime, store, and (with `--all`) auth, registry, tunnel, tooling, plugins, globals, sandbox, and full manifest-compat
  swift-registry   Configure Swift Package Manager to use LPM as a package registry (SE-0292)
  mcp              Manage MCP servers (setup, remove, status)
  use              Install, pin, and manage Node.js versions (e.g., lpm use node@22)
  env              Manage project environment variables and secrets
  run              Run script(s) from package.json
  exec             Run a project-local binary from node_modules/.bin
  dlx              Run a package binary without installing it into the project
  deploy           Materialize a single workspace member's deploy closure into a self-contained output directory ready for `COPY --from=pruned` in a Dockerfile
  approve-scripts  Review and approve packages whose lifecycle scripts were blocked by LPM's default-deny security posture
  patch            Generate a local patch for an installed package, `patch-package` style
  patch-commit     Finalize a patch staging directory created by `lpm patch`
  patch-remove     Remove one or more registered local patches
  sbom             Generate a Software Bill of Materials from lpm.lock
  filter           Preview the workspace package set that a `--filter` expression would select. Read-only — never executes scripts or modifies state
  plugin           Manage tool plugins (list, outdated, update, remove)
  lint             Lint source files (powered by Oxlint, lazy-downloaded on first use)
  fmt              Format source files (powered by Biome, lazy-downloaded on first use)
  check            Type-check the project (runs tsc --noEmit by default)
  bundle           Bundle the project with Rolldown through an LPM-owned command surface
  pack             Build package-oriented library output through a stable LPM command surface
  test             Run tests (auto-detects vitest/jest/mocha)
  bench            Run benchmarks (auto-detects vitest bench)
  ci               Frozen install for CI
  dev              Start the dev server with optional HTTPS, tunnel, and network features
  cert             Manage local HTTPS certificates (status, trust, uninstall, generate, rotate, reconcile)
  why              Explain why a package is installed
  graph            Visualize the dependency graph (tree, DOT, Mermaid, JSON, stats, HTML) [aliases: ls]
  ports            Manage dev service ports and inspect listening processes
  hosts            Manage LPM hosts-file entries
  proxy            Manage the local-domain proxy daemon
  tunnel           Expose a local port to the internet via LPM tunnel
  migrate          Migrate from npm/yarn/pnpm/bun to LPM
  self-update      Update LPM to the latest version
  completions      Generate a shell completion script
  schema           Emit the JSON Schema for an LPM config file
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -V
          Print version and exit.
          
          Accepts `-V` and `-v`. Long `--version` is handled before clap parsing so subcommands like `info` and `download` can safely use `--version <package-version>`.
          
          [aliases: -v]

      --token <TOKEN>
          Use a specific auth token instead of the stored one

      --registry <REGISTRY>
          Override the registry URL
          
          [env: LPM_REGISTRY_URL=]

      --json
          Output as JSON (for CI/scripting)

      --verbose
          Show verbose output (debug logging).
          
          Long form only — `-v` was reclaimed for `--version` to match npm/pnpm/yarn convention.

      --insecure
          Allow insecure HTTP connections to non-localhost registries

      --color <COLOR>
          Color output mode. `auto` (default) honors `FORCE_COLOR`, `NO_COLOR`, then falls back to stdout TTY detection

          Possible values:
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even when stdout isn't a TTY
          - auto:   Respect `FORCE_COLOR` / `NO_COLOR`, then fall back to stdout TTY detection. Default
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
